prompt:
Design brief — your own take on this character. A full-body vertical 2:3 (1024×1536) character card image of an adult woman — the personification of the element Sulfur (황) itself — the sovereign of the Sulfur Nation. A female character who IS the element; her costume, ornaments and colors carry the element’s traits. Age: late twenties — a graceful grown-up face with soft, smooth contours; no wrinkles, folds or under-eye bags.

You design her yourself: invent her face, eye colour, hairstyle, makeup, expression, pose and setting as a fresh, original take — do not follow any earlier design of this character. Her hair colour and costume are NOT free: take them from our designs below.

Style (fixed): A Japanese anime key visual with a painterly finish: an anime-style character with an elegant adult anime face, large expressive eyes, a small nose and mouth, fine coloured linework and soft cel-to-painted shading with painted highlights in the hair and fabric. Behind her, a richly painted background with layered painterly colour, subtle visible brushwork, atmospheric perspective and cinematic depth. Luminous, rich colours; crisp focal details on the face and costume, softer painted edges toward the distance. No flat single-tone cel shading, photographic appearance, semi-realistic face or plastic 3D-render finish.

Inspiration only — her element: sulfur: bright lemon-yellow crystals blooming at volcanic vents, burning at night with an eerie electric-blue flame, choking yellow fumes, brimstone-and-hellfire legend, one third of black gunpowder, the toughness of vulcanized black rubber, black basalt underfoot. Palette: sulfur yellow, eerie blue flame, volcanic basalt black, ember red.

World (fixed): around 1850, a sulfur mine and a gunpowder mill: heaps of yellow ore burning in kilns, brass-bound powder kegs in a magazine, a vulcanizing works for rubber with steaming presses. Her costume and setting belong to this world.

Costume (choose one of ours, then add your own idea): pick ONE of these costume shapes from our set and keep its overall silhouette — 1) a heavy leather work apron with rolled sleeves, a tool harness and one big gauntlet glove — a hands-on engineer's shape; 2) a cropped flight jacket, goggles on her head, crossing harness straps and a long scarf streaming in the wind — an airborne shape; 3) a long leather coat with a bandolier of glass vials, brass goggles and long gloves — a mysterious experimenter's shape; 4) a clockwork gear rig worn on her back over a fitted vest, small brass fittings on arms and legs — the machinery makes the shape; 5) a sleeveless work vest, thick leather gloves, soot-stained trousers and boots — a furnace stoker's rugged shape. Then add one signature idea of your own drawn from her element, built into the construction of the outfit itself rather than as a print or a loose accessory — e.g. plates or cloth layered like crystals, scales or flames, a hem or sleeve cut into a shape from her element. Build it in this world's materials and our colours below.

Costume colours (ours): sulfur yellow, eerie blue flame, volcanic basalt black, ember red.

Hair colour (fixed — ours): volcanic basalt-black hair tipped with crystalline sulfur-yellow. Keep exactly this hair colour; only the hairstyle is yours.

Exposure (fixed): bold — her outfit shows skin by design (a deep neckline, bare shoulders or arms, a high slit or short hem); intimate areas covered.

Face proportions: a short midface and a soft, gently rounded jawline with a small soft chin; any crown or headpiece sits above her hairline. Her eyes keep the shape and size described above.

Composition: vertical 2:3 full-body framing with modest headroom and clear space below the boots — the whole figure from the top of her head or headpiece to both feet stays inside the frame, occupying about four-fifths of the image height, with the same camera distance in every world; her hands stay inside the frame. Camera level with her face with natural portrait perspective; her head level, chin neither raised nor tucked — no upward perspective on her face, no wide-angle distortion, no low angle, no close crop.

If you have already drawn a free design of her in this session, make this one clearly different — another face and hairstyle (the same hair colour), another costume shape with another signature idea, another pose and setting.

Write your own detailed image prompt from this brief, then draw it. One figure only, natural hands with five fingers; no text or numbers except her element's own chemical symbol (S) and atomic number (16) — and those only as part of the scene: engraved, embroidered or glowing on her costume, a banner, a sign or a machine, never as a floating label, corner badge, periodic-table tile, caption or overlay on the picture; no logo or watermark.
